markdown_report:
The best first experiment is **gated recent-and-repeated interest SASRec with multi-negative supervision**. It targets weak adjacent-interest recommendations, excessive influence from older interests, and poor lower-tail score separation. Gains remain hypotheses until measured by pinned macro validation HR@10.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights motivate the design: (1) SASRec already learns useful ordering, so preserve its collaborative pathway; positive mean margins support this conservative starting point. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive errors and a −0.4812 margin p10, motivating stronger ranking supervision. (3) Users favor recent, repeated interests over loose historical associations, motivating explicit local-context conditioning. These observations do not establish compatibility or unmet need.

Three literature insights organize the alternatives: (1) LSTASRec separates persistent and transient interests [2], suggesting a lightweight gated branch. (2) gSASRec motivates revisiting single-negative supervision [3], while R²NS cautions that immediate hard mining can hurt [4]. (3) TedRec and WhitenRec motivate selective text use but warn that semantic similarity alone lacks discrimination [5,6]; pretrained results do not establish scratch-text gains here.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intent | Long/short extractors [2] | Causal recent/repeated pooling | Preferences remain latent |
| Supervision | Generalized BCE [3] | Uniform 16-negative softmax | False negatives remain |
| Content | Text–ID fusion [5,6] | Bounded scratch-text residual | Compatibility unverified |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are 0–10; difficulty increases with implementation effort. Each entry gives a positive (+) and negative (−) reason.

1. **Gated intent ranking, selected.** Originality 4: + integrates context and ranking; − familiar components. Potential 8: + extensible intent conditioning; − benchmark dependence. User alignment 8: + targets stale and adjacent interests; − cannot verify satisfaction. Model alignment 8: + directly trains competing scores; − margins may not generalize. Difficulty 4: + small SASRec extension; − causal pooling needs care.
2. **Sixteen-negative softmax alone.** Originality 2: + clean hypothesis; − established technique. Potential 6: + reusable baseline; − limited architectural insight. User alignment 4: + stronger discrimination; − no explicit temporal correction. Model alignment 8: + addresses weak margins; − random negatives may be easy. Difficulty 2: + vectorized loss; − extra scoring cost.
3. **Bounded scratch-text residual.** Originality 4: + task-compatible adaptation; − familiar fusion. Potential 7: + content-sensitive matching; − sparse supervision. User alignment 7: + may capture specific formats; − wording cannot certify compatibility. Model alignment 5: + additional discrimination; − may amplify confusion. Difficulty 6: + compact encoder; − tokenization and serving changes.

**Selected algorithm.** At each causal position, gate SASRec features with an exponentially weighted recent-window pool; boost repeated item occurrences using prefix-only counts. Optimize the fused representation against one positive and 16 uniform unseen negatives. This encourages recent/repeated evidence and directly targets weak separation. Ablate pooling, loss, and their combination; select solely by prescribed macro validation HR@10. Preserve all four routes, seeds, predictor parity, and diagnostic contracts.

idea.description: Extend each category's SASRec with one causal recent-interest residual. Pool the last five available item embeddings with exponential recency weights multiplied by a bounded function of each item's occurrence count in the observed prefix. A learned scalar gate combines this pool with SASRec's existing representation. Train candidate scores using 16 uniformly sampled negatives per valid position.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale interests and loosely adjacent recommendations displacing direct current-interest matches. Explicit recent and repeated evidence addresses both patterns without claiming that purchases reveal satisfaction or equipment compatibility. Multi-negative supervision targets the measured weak separation, especially Electronics' negative margin p10 and 14.95% sampled ordering-error rate. The observed embedding similarity near the mapped zero-cosine baseline does not justify prioritizing collapse regularization.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, existing splits, all four category routes, and trial-local artifacts. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS, whose host default is 200. Pool only prefix items at every training position; count repeats only inside that prefix. Use window size 5, initial recency decay 0.8, repeat multiplier 1 + log(1 + max(count - 1, 0)), and normalize pooling weights. Project the pool to SASRec's hidden dimension and use fused = LayerNorm(sasrec + sigmoid(gate([sasrec, pool])) * projection(pool)); initialize the gate bias to -2. These are starting hyperparameters, not measured optima. Score positive and negative items with the same trained item embeddings. Exclude padding, the positive, and observed training-history items from negatives; handle tiny eligible catalogs without infinite rejection loops. Use a numerically stable cross-entropy over one positive and 16 negatives. Compare baseline, pooling only, loss only, and their combination within the shared GPU budget; report category HR@10 alongside the selection macro average. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the gate, projection, normalization, and pooling exactly. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Make view.log2feats return fused features and view.predict_score use deployed scoring. Return measured metrics with definitions; unavailable category breakdowns should explicitly state unavailable rather than infer categories. Measure margin diagnostics with a fixed negative protocol across variants because changing sampling changes their interpretation. No pretrained weights or additional data are required.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    initialize SASRec and recent_pool_gate with training seed 42
    for epoch in configured_epochs:
        for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
            base = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
            for valid causal position t:
                prefix = sequence[:t+1] without padding
                window = last_5(prefix)
                weights = recency_decay(window) * bounded_repeat_weight(prefix, window)
                recent[t] = weighted_mean(item_emb(window), weights)
            fused = layer_norm(base + sigmoid(gate(concat(base, recent))) * project(recent))
            negatives = sample_16_uniform_eligible_items_per_position()
            logits = dot(fused, item_emb(concat(positive, negatives)))
            loss = cross_entropy(logits[valid_positions], positive_index=0)
            optimize(loss)
    save model configuration and weights beneath trial directory
    emit predictor implementing identical fused scoring
compare authorized variants with pinned validation macro HR@10
retain the best validated configuration across all four routes

originality.positive: Combines explicit causal recent/repeated evidence with richer ranking supervision in a small extension suited to the observed failure patterns.
originality.negative: Gated interest fusion and multi-negative objectives are established mechanisms; novelty is primarily the task-specific combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a tractable foundation for studying when recent evidence should override broad historical affinity.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may depend on history density, repeat frequency, and evaluation candidate sampling; compatibility and satisfaction remain unobserved.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec embeddings, encoder, category routing, and dot-product scoring with a small residual branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Prefix-safe repeat counts, eligible negative sampling, and exact training/inference parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal self-attention for sequential next-item recommendation.
Provides the collaborative sequence encoder retained by the proposal.
limitations: Does not establish that historical affinity identifies current unmet needs or equipment compatibility.

related_work.title: LSTASRec (2025 preprint)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separate long- and short-term interest extraction with adaptive fusion.
limitations: Its reported results do not establish improvements on this pinned benchmark.
The proposed lightweight pooling branch is an adaptation, not a reproduction.

related_work.title: gSASRec extended abstract
contributions: Examines overconfidence from sampled binary cross-entropy and motivates generalized BCE.
Supports investigating the training objective rather than attributing every failure to encoder capacity.
limitations: Generalized BCE and the proposed sampled-softmax objective are different methods.
Objective changes require independent validation on the requested four categories.

related_work.title: R²NS, WWW 2026
contributions: The supplied summary supports uniform-negative warm-up and progressive hard-negative sampling.
Motivates avoiding immediate deterministic hardest-negative mining.
limitations: Does not guarantee that harder negatives improve this task.
Unobserved items can still be false negatives.

related_work.title: TedRec
contributions: Combines text and collaborative ID sequences through frequency-domain operations.
limitations: Uses pretrained language representations, so reported gains do not validate the allowed scratch-trained text alternative.

related_work.title: WhitenRec
contributions: Highlights discrimination limitations in text representations for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Semantic similarity does not certify functional compatibility or a valid next-item transition.
